subject: Re: GritWorks MSA - Output rights & training opt-out
content:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@gritworks.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@gritworks.com, legal@gritworks.com
Date: Tue, 2 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GritWorks MSA redlines - output & model reuse

Sean —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Legal has circulated a focused set of redlines on IP and productization. Two items are blocking procurement sign-off:

1) Output ownership: GritWorks requests explicit assignment of output for Customer Content so we can ship models and derivative features to our customers without downstream restrictions.
2) Training opt-out: we need the ability to opt specific datasets out of any training/feedback usage by Redwood (including internal retrain pipelines) and a technical control to enforce that.

I'm attaching the redlines (short summary is inline in the doc). Can your legal and product teams confirm feasibility and proposed language? Procurement is targeting a PO this month if we can close.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of Platform, GritWorks

--Attachment: GritWorks_MSA_redlines_v3.docx (document stub)

Subject: Re: GritWorks MSA redlines - output & model reuse

Elena —

Appreciate the clear summary. Looping in legal (Laura) and product (Vanessa + Ben) to scope the asks. High level thoughts from our side:

- Output ownership: we typically grant customers broad rights to use and distribute outputs generated from their data, but assignment (title transfer) is unusual at the MSA layer. We can add a clear customer license for outputs and carve out telemetry/aggregate usage, but full assignment language requires escalation.

- Training opt-out: we support per-customer and per-tenant opt-out for training/feedback on Hosted and Dedicated. For Private deployments, opt-out semantics differ since the control plane may be customer-managed. We need to capture the exact enforcement mechanism (API toggle, contract flag, and evidence logs).

Action items: Vanessa, can you confirm technical enforcement and whether we can provide audit logs showing opt-out enforcement? Laura, can you propose contract language that gives GritWorks the usage rights they need without exposing Redwood to model IP leakage concerns?

I'll set a quick sync if helpful.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@gritworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Oct 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GritWorks MSA redlines - output & model reuse

Elena / team —

Quick product note on enforcement:

- Hosted API: we already maintain a per-customer training opt-out flag. When set, customer requests are not written to training pipelines and are excluded from telemetry used for model updates. We can expose an API endpoint and a monthly audit CSV showing counts of excluded requests.

- Dedicated: the flag can be managed via the Dedicated console (admin-only). We can add a webhook that fires on opt-out changes for auditability.

- Private/VPC: if the control plane is customer-managed, opt-out is enforced locally; our Private package includes a toggle but evidence depends on deployment architecture.

Caveat: opt-out prevents Redwood from using the content to improve shared models; it does not change downstream output rights unless specified in contract language. If GritWorks wants explicit assignment of outputs (title), that has productization implications (we need to restrict model reuse and may need escrow/segregation of derivative artifacts).

I can produce a short technical appendix showing the API/webhook and an example audit CSV.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Product, Platform — Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@gritworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Oct 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GritWorks MSA redlines - output & model reuse

Elena / GritWorks counsel —

Thanks for the redlines. We've reviewed and propose the following compromise language and controls to balance customer productization needs with our IP and safety obligations:

1) Outputs: Redwood will grant GritWorks an exclusive, perpetual, transferable license to use, reproduce, and sublicense Outputs derived solely from GritWorks Customer Content, subject to Redwood's retained rights to use aggregated, de-identified metrics and improvement code. We cannot provide assignment of underlying model weights or technologies.

2) Training opt-out: Redwood will implement a contractual and technical opt-out for GritWorks Customer Content. When opt-out is enabled, Redwood will not use that content in supervised model training or reinforcement pipelines for shared models. Redwood will, however, retain operational logs and non-content telemetry for debugging and service improvements (aggregated).

3) Audit & evidence: Redwood will provide a monthly audit report (CSV) delivered to a pre-agreed S3/Drive location, and maintain an immutable event log for the opt-out toggle for 12 months. For Dedicated/Private modalities, audit scope will be adjusted to reflect control-plane ownership.

4) Escrow / derivative segregation: If GritWorks requires full title to derived datasets or model snapshots built from their content, we will treat that as a professional services engagement with associated costs (data isolation, reproducibility runbooks, and potential escrow fees).

Next steps:
- If GritWorks accepts 1–3, legal can prepare a redline that replaces the requested assignment with the exclusive license language and the opt-out/audit commitments above.
- If GritWorks insists on assignment of model derivatives, we'll need to scope SOW/pricing.

We can have a 30-minute call to finalize contract text — propose Fri 5 Oct 10:00 PT.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

Laura / Sean —

Thanks — that compromise looks workable. A few clarifying points from procurement before we lock language:

- The license needs to be transferable to our downstream customers and partners; make sure sublicense rights are explicit.
- Event log retention for opt-out: can you extend from 12 months to 24 months? We have audits that may go back further.
- For Dedicated deployments, we need the webhook audit to include a SHA256 of the opt-out payload and a timestamp to verify integrity.

We can take the SOW conversation offline if needed, but for the base PO we need the exclusive license + 24-month log retention. Can you confirm by EOD so procurement can issue the PO?

Best,
Elena
